page: Microsoft Azure D32nds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dndv6 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by an Intel processor, accompanied by 128.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual processor. The server does not include GPU acceleration hardware.

The instance comes equipped with 1890 GB of high-throughput local NVMe SSD storage and offers compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. The underlying architecture is designated as network-optimized, facilitating data-intensive inter-node communication. Standard deployment does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network routing or allocated public addressing for external ingress.

By coupling 32 dedicated execution threads with an integrated 1890 GB NVMe SSD volume, the configuration yields cost efficiency for data-heavy workloads requiring fast temporary storage without provisioning dedicated external block volumes. Best-fit use cases include transactional and relational databases, high-capacity caching systems, big data analytics engines, continuous integration build clusters, and general enterprise backend workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D32nds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance in the Dndv6 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on an Intel architecture, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage, accommodating I/O-intensive tasks directly on high-speed ephemeral disks. Lacking discrete GPUs, the instance focuses on balanced central processing and network-optimized communication. Resource density provides solid cost efficiency for environments needing substantial compute and high local IOPS without the cost of provisioning auxiliary block volumes for temporary storage. Recommended workloads include transactional databases, high-throughput web serving, big data processing, enterprise backend applications, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
